notes.title: SimplePlanes VR is now available
notes.content:
After far too many late nights of caffeine-infused coding and 3D modeling, we are proud to present [url=https://www.simpleplanes.com/vr/buy]SimplePlanes VR[/url]. Strap a VR headset to your face and grab the stick and throttle in front of you to fly. Flip switches, push buttons, crank levers, slide throttles, and so much more. Download community-made aircraft without leaving the comfort of your VR headset. SimplePlanes VR is the most feature-packed VR flight sim you'll find for the meager cost of a gourmet sandwich. We hope you enjoy your flight!

[i]SimplePlanes VR is a standalone game and does not require SimplePlanes. However, if you own SimplePlanes, then purchasing SPVR will unlock VR mode in your original SimplePlanes so you can easily switch to VR mode and see how your builds are looking in VR.[/i]

[url=https://www.simpleplanes.com/vr/buy][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40965650/0a8592e4c696ac3b530493d894e49628e202f518.png[/img][/url]

[h3]LAUNCH TRAILER[/h3]
[url=https://youtu.be/yT6TV0_XaDU][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40965650/73f503a4aec2c9c481ba562aa87c10b0310830ac.jpg[/img][/url]

[h3]KEY FEATURES[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fully immersive cockpits and virtual controls that you can reach out and grab with your hands
[*] Download and fly any number of crafts from SimplePlanes.com for free
[*] Escort a bomber, torpedo a WW2 destroyer, dogfight enemy aircraft, obliterate a convoy, and several more combat challenges are included
[*] Fly around in sandbox mode and engage neutral aircraft and ships or spawn enemy aircraft to dogfight whenever it suits your fancy
[*] Explore islands and airports to unlock secret locations
[*] Includes several air and car racecourses to compete against A.I. opponents
[*] One of the very few flight sims available for Oculus Quest, and the only one that includes helicopters and such a wide variety of aircraft!
[/list]

[h3]THE JUNDROO MACHINE[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40965650/d4eab39199711d7dd3f12fd10ba1c943b010fcf0.png[/img]

We've got the caffeine covered. If you can help provide some positive energy then you can help keep the Jundroo machine running and churning out games and updates. Positive energy can take many forms:

[b]1) Playing our games, of course![/b]  
  
[b]2) Sharing SimplePlanes VR on social media[/b]
  
[i]Thanks for playing and thanks for supporting our small indie game dev studio![/i]

-The Jundroo Team

notes.title: Ion Engine in SimpleRockets 2
notes.content:
The tyrannical [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsiolkovsky_rocket_equation]Tsiolkovsky rocket equation[/url] cannot be avoided. The only way for rockets to accelerate in space is by expelling some of their mass. Most engines do this with combustion, which expels huge amounts of fuel mass at a respectable velocity. This gives great acceleration (and an impressive fireball), but very poor specific impulse. Specific impulse is like gas mileage for rocket engines. 

Ion engines, on the other hand, take a different approach.

[img]https://imgur.com/Laj5Adk.gif[/img]

They shoot out a minuscule amount of fuel mass, but they do it at [i]insane[/i] velocities. Around 40 [b]kilometers[/b] per second (90,000mph). This results in a force that is about the equivalent of lifting a piece of paper into the air. That's not very impressive, but they make up for it by taking their time with their fuel. Ion engines can "burn" for weeks, so this small force can add up to an extremely impressive delta-V. 

This little satellite I made has a delta-V of 14,533 m/s and a burn time of about 72 hours. 

[img]https://imgur.com/2PYpreO.png[/img]

Here are the details:

[list]
[*] Thrust: [b]0.050 kN[/b] (Yep, that's right, just fifty Newtons)
[*] Mass: [b]50 kg[/b]
[*] Price: [b]$100,000[/b]
[*] Specific Impulse: [b]11,515 s[/b]
[*] Fuel Type: [b]Xenon[/b]
[*] Electrical Consumption: [b]100kW[/b]
[*] Height: [b]0.25 m[/b]
[*] Diameter: [b]0.6 m[/b]
[*] Max Gimbal Angle: [b]0 degrees[/b]
[/list]
Given the extremely long burn times, these engines aren't very useful when playing the game at normal speed. This weekend I've been prototyping how to use these engines while playing the game at up to 1,000x fast-forward mode. It makes playing with these engines far more enjoyable.

notes.title: Cargo Bays in SimpleRockets 2
notes.content:
The cargo bay will open the door to many possibilities. The most obvious being the space shuttle. There are many more possibilities, but it really hinges on your creativity. I know the creativity of our players is far greater than my own and I can't wait to see what you do with them.

[img]https://imgur.com/jEMZUX0.gif[/img]

The cargo bay is our most complicated procedural part. It can be resized just like the fuel tank, so it can take on an infinite number of shapes. You can also change the angle the doors open as well as their speed. 

[img]https://imgur.com/HE2Jhj1.gif[/img]

My son just pointed out to me that the green one looks like a coffin. That wasn't the intention, but just add that to the list of things you can make with the cargo bay part. You could also use it to house custom-made, retractable landing gear. Or you could make a bomb bay (we don't have bombs, but you can pretty much make anything with the fuel tank part). Or set the open angle to zero and use it as a hollow fuselage. 

Here are the part details:

[list]
[*] Mass: [b]Your[/b]
[*] Price: [b]Heart's[/b]
[*] Size: [b]Desire[/b]
[*] Max Open Angle: [b]0 to 150 degrees[/b]
[*] Opening Speed: [b]10% to 250%[/b]
[/list]
Also, in case you missed it, [url=https://imgur.com/a/ixRPWKc]here are some screenshots[/url] of a Space Shuttle that Kevin made a few weeks ago. (The cargo bay has changed a lot since then).

Now that I have you, I should mention a little something about our launch date. Today we looked over the remaining tasks and the long list of bugs and we came to the conclusion that we are extremely unlikely to launch by end of summer (Sept 22nd). We are now putting our launch date in October. I am confident this will be the last slippage of schedule. If I'm wrong, I will eat black licorice. I hate black licorice.

notes.title: Apex I Engine in SimpleRockets 2
notes.content:
Our newest engine, the Apex I is an absolute beast. It's heavy, expensive, and drinks RP-1 like there's no tomorrow, but it will have the power to get even your most poorly engineered contraptions into space.

[img]https://imgur.com/kqWFSWy.gif[/img]

It dwarfs the [url=https://www.simplerockets.com/Blog/View/437/Introducing-the-Mage-I-Engine]Mage I[/url] engine in size, power, and visuals.

[img]https://imgur.com/YbDkQmp.png[/img]

Here are the details:

[list]
[*] Thrust: [b]3,200 kN[/b]
[*] Mass: [b]3,500 kg[/b]
[*] Price: [b]$8,500,000[/b]
[*] Height: [b]4.2 m[/b]
[*] Diameter: [b]3.0 m[/b]
[*] Max Gimbal Angle: [b]2.5 degrees[/b]
[*] Fuel Consumption: [b]1,350 L/s[/b]
[*] Specific Impulse: [b]298 s[/b]
[/list]

Here's a [url=https://imgur.com/75pZ2Pl]bonus shot[/url] of it in a highly ill-advised use case.

[i]Can anyone guess the inspiration behind this engine? I'll give you a hint, if you are on a PC, the name of the engine is on your keyboard...[/i]

notes.title: Pixie Engine in SR2
notes.content:
*Note: Check the [url=https://www.simplerockets.com/Forums/View/496/SimpleRockets-2-FAQ]FAQ here[/url] before asking questions.*

We've just completed development of the second engine in SR2. The Pixie engine is a much smaller alternative to the [url=https://www.simplerockets.com/Blog/View/437/Introducing-the-Mage-I-Engine]Mage engine[/url] with far better gas mileage. This makes it suitable for those second stages destined for Smoon. With an accordingly lower thrust, it is also a lot easier to land on a low-G planetary body without getting into an endless cycle of up-and-down that I often find myself in when trying to land with a Mage engine.

[img]https://imgur.com/MMzUYRq.gif[/img]

Here are the details:

[list]
[*] Thrust: [b]50 kN[/b]
[*] Mass: [b]75 kg[/b] (165 lbs)
[*] Price: [b]$150k[/b]
[*] Height: [b]1.0 m[/b] (3.2 ft)
[*] Diameter: [b]0.7 m[/b] (2.3 ft)
[*] Max Gimbal Angle: [b]10 degrees[/b]
[*] Fuel Consumption: [b]15 L/s[/b]
[*] [wiki=en]Specific impulse[/wiki]: [b]339 s[/b]
[*] Max Torque: [b]5 Nm[/b]
[/list]
Here's a [url=https://imgur.com/58V5XjR]bonus shot of it in action[/url].

Also, I just wanted to let everyone know that I'm going to start posting blog updates every other week instead of every week. It's been fun, but these posts take a lot of time to put together and as we continue to slip further and further behind schedule, I need to use any extra time I can find to focus on development. I hope you understand!
